questions.prompt: A cylinder needs slow extension and fast retraction. Which control arrangement allows different speeds?
questions.answer: Independent speed control in each direction
options: Independent speed control in each direction
One fixed speed in both directions
questions.explanation: Separate flow controls allow extension and retraction speeds to be adjusted independently.

reviewCue.text: Review C209 Pneumatic Systems.pdf, slide 87. Look for Independent Speed Control, slide 87.
reviewCue.excerpt:
INDEPENDENT SPEED CONTROL
• This is when an actuators speed must be adjusted 
independently in each direction.
• Slow approach/fast reset
• Matching retraction and extension speeds.
• In pneumatic systems, slowing a cylinder is 
achieved by restricting the exhaust air flow rather 
than the incoming air.
• This technique is called meter-out control, where 
the flow control valve is placed on the exhaust 
side of the actuator.
• By switching to a slower flow control speed, the 
cylinder’s motion becomes smoother and more 
controlled during deceleration.
87
